the number of hidden units in a neural network is the most important determinant of the number of localist units that are learned.

the number of emergent codes on the hidden layers of a feed-forward network is determined by the number of hidden neurons, the size of input space, the number of training examples, and the sparsity and noise of the data.

local codes can emerge from feedforward PDP networks and the number of localist codes that emerge is a function of the size of input space, number of examples seen, sparsity of input and the number of hidden neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the emergence of localist coding in feed-forward neural networks.
the emergence of localist representations in feed-forward neural networks.
the question of when localist representations emerge in feed-forward NNs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the emergence of local codes in feed-forward neural networks depends on the number of neurons in the hidden layer, the number of training examples, the number of classes in the output data and the sparsity (or density) of the data.
“localist codes can emerge in feed-forward neural networks under the correct conditions”.
localist coding is not a necessary condition of PDP theory.

local codes are not an exception but the default in feed-forward NNs.
the number of hidden units in a feed-forward network is an important factor in determining whether or not local codes emerge.
